findings.title: Everything Everywhere: Systemic Data Exposure in Supabase Apps
findings.summary_md: UpGuard Research (Greg Pollock) scanned roughly 300,000 domains showing signs of Supabase use and identified 16,326 databases exposing readable tables. Over half carried indicators of PII, with smaller subsets exposing passwords and authentication tokens and a very small set of plausible credit card data. The report attributes exposure to missing or ineffective row-level security and misuse of public keys, and notes tables created programmatically through the API do not enable RLS by default. UpGuard notified application owners where deeper analysis found significant exposure.

findings.title: Statement on CVE-2025-48757
findings.summary_md: Matt Palmer's disclosure statement documents the original researcher finding of systemic Row Level Security misconfiguration in Lovable-built apps backed by Supabase, first discovered March 20, 2025. A scan completed March 21, 2025 found 303 exposed endpoints across 170 of 1,645 showcase projects, about 10.3 percent, and the CVE was published May 29, 2025 after a 45-day window with a CVSS v3.1 vector of AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N. The statement also records public exploitation of the same flaw on April 14, 2025.

findings.title: What 2,000 Exposed Vibe-Coded Apps Reveal About the Limits of Most Security Stacks
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News covered Red Access's Shadow Builders report, which identified more than 380,000 publicly accessible web assets across leading vibe-coding platforms. Roughly 5,000 looked corporate and more than 2,000 exposed sensitive corporate, operational, or personal data with no exploitation required. The piece argues EDR, DLP, and CASB miss these applications because the risk sits in the gaps between those control layers.

findings.title: Hacking Moltbook: The AI Social Network Any Human Can Control
findings.summary_md: Wiz Research disclosed a misconfigured Supabase database behind Moltbook, a social network for AI agents, that granted unauthenticated read and write access to all platform data. The exposure included 1.5 million API authentication tokens, 35,000 email addresses, private messages, and roughly 4.75 million records; the maintainer applied fixes within hours of contact starting January 31, 2026. The post describes the recurring pattern of Supabase keys in client-side JavaScript without RLS in vibe-coded applications.

findings.title: Supabase Security Retro: 2025
findings.summary_md: Supabase CISO Bil Harmer and CEO Paul Copplestone review 2025 platform security changes. RLS is enabled by default only for tables created via the dashboard Table Editor, not for tables created programmatically, and Event Triggers plus email alerts and Security Advisors were added to detect tables without RLS. New revocable publishable and secret API keys replace legacy JWT-based anon and service_role keys, which will be removed in late 2026, and the post states application-level security remains each customer's responsibility.
